diagrams.title: From Offer Page to Hidden Spread
diagrams.subtitle: The five-step pay-per-call lane check practitioners run before buying traffic
diagrams.caption: A buyer pays a fixed price for a live inbound call that clears pre-agreed rules on duration, geography and hours; the operator keeps the spread between traffic cost and call price.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Figures are attributed practitioner claims: TrackDrive's $50 revenue, $35 payout, $15 margin split; Ringba's $25 call costing $2 to generate; Leadbase's three-of-ten paid ratio turning a $50 cost into $150. Results vary by vertical and buyer.
diagrams.note: Sources: WordsAtScale (DJFaYJ3O7aU), Ringba (4kaOQgGnpJo), Leadbase (ewNftdwX784), TrackDrive (V1FTIO7peWA, _h1_mcKPGjY), Start & Grow Your Business (8qGNYXEyrqI).

stages.label: Read every line of the offer page
stages.detail: Check minimum call length, buyer hours, hold period, and who owns the buyer before sending a single call (WordsAtScale).

stages.label: Front the network number with your own tracking
stages.detail: Put your own tracking number in front of the network's number to verify every call and catch skimming (Ringba).

stages.label: Model the worst-case paid ratio
stages.detail: A buyer paying for three of ten calls turns a $50 cost into $150 per paid call (Leadbase).

stages.label: Qualify each call on duration rules
stages.detail: A call that meets the rules is qualified and paid; one that does not is unpaid. Callers stay on the line a minute or two (TrackDrive; Start & Grow).

stages.label: Pocket the spread and keep it hidden
stages.detail: $50 revenue minus $35 payout leaves $15 per call; once a campaign works, never let the buyer see a $25 call that cost $2 (TrackDrive; Ringba).

diagrams.title: One-to-One Consent Readiness Funnel
diagrams.subtitle: Where lead-gen operators stood before January 27 enforcement
diagrams.caption: Most operators were still testing consent capture, and Eric Troutman read only two of ten circulating one-to-one forms as passing.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The first, second, third and fifth stages are percentage shares from the ActiveProspect and boberdoo webinar poll taken 111 days before January 27 enforcement. The fourth stage expresses Troutman's 'probably only 2 of 10' as a share. Agent CRM and Revenx report the rule vacated, so regulatory direction is contested among practitioners.
diagrams.note: Sources: ActiveProspect, Inc. (uXTg2yB_ZTM), Eric Troutman via Seasalt AI (KBFaRW7QmVQ), TechMarketer (B9lfPgUUls0), Calldrive (jHMaZ1k0rpY).

stages.label: Operators testing consent capture
stages.conversion: Largest bloc in the ActiveProspect and boberdoo poll
stages.detail: Single select for each item, no select all, and no pre-check (TechMarketer).

stages.label: Operators with an idea only
stages.conversion: Planning stage, no live forms yet
stages.detail: Bid per company, not per whole lead; with 15 buyers the form shows 15 checkboxes (ActiveProspect, Inc.).

stages.label: Operators fully ready
stages.conversion: Consent records producible by buyer and seller
stages.detail: Calldrive pairs a consent token with IP address and a video of the form fill.

stages.label: Circulating forms that pass review
stages.detail: Lead sellers create the risk, but buyers bear it, with indemnity flowing back.

stages.label: Operators not yet started
stages.detail: Quoted exposure runs $500 to $2,000 per text or call violation (Amy Chan via Seasalt AI).

diagrams.title: Why the IVR Gate Protects Margin
diagrams.subtitle: TrackDrive's 100-call example of paying on every call versus qualified calls only
diagrams.caption: An IVR sorts callers on the attribute that decides payout before any buyer phone rings; paying a publisher on unqualified calls drains margin from 30% to 12.5%.
diagrams.assumptions_note: TrackDrive states 100 calls, 80 qualifying, a $1,200 (30%) margin falling to $500 (12.5%) when all 100 are paid. The 20 non-qualifying calls and the $700 gap are arithmetic on those stated figures. Ringba's debt IVR forwards only callers with more than $10,000 in unsecured credit card debt.
diagrams.note: Sources: TrackDrive (yYZ5s6jFzQs), Ringba / Jordan Soto (4dnXkZ7u6zw), Carlos Corona (tf4AieS7Mhc).

diagrams.title: The RTB Call Timing Envelope
diagrams.subtitle: Ping, timeout and billing-pad windows practitioners configure
diagrams.caption: Call RTB is ping-post for live phone calls: bids return and the call routes to the best expected payout before the phone rings, with failover so an unanswered winner never kills a paid call.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Ping-to-route is 'a couple hundred milliseconds, always under one second' (Ringba), plotted as 0.2 s typical. RingbaX values come from Ringba's seller ring tree recipe; the 5-second timeout and 8-second pad come from ceohec's Retreaver build. Platform defaults differ.

bars.label: Ping-to-route decision
bars.display: A couple hundred ms; always under 1 s

bars.label: Connect lag and billing pad
bars.display: 3-5 s connect lag; pad +8 s (120 s becomes 128 s)

diagrams.title: The Ping-Post Exclusionary Auction
diagrams.subtitle: Four gates between a non-contact ping and a paid PII post
diagrams.caption: A non-contact ping fires simultaneously to every eligible buyer; the best bid minus margin returns to the seller, and the PII post lands only after the buyer returns success.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Timeouts of 15 s ping and 30 s post are boberdoo's typical windows; another boberdoo setup returns a generic unmatched after 20 seconds. The $10 bid minus $2 margin and the 15% refund cap over 30 days are boberdoo examples, not fixed rules.
diagrams.note: Sources: boberdoo.com (yCAVYNpSdZI, YLw0lKsOayk, lpWTQpnduYo, EKrBDZYFq2A), Scott Hoffman and Brett of boberdoo, Lead Prosper.

nodes.question: Does the buyer hold an active account, funds and a matching filter set?
nodes.fail_action: Excluded from the ping; extra fields that trip the filter set are common.

nodes.question: Did the buyer bid inside the ping window (15 s typical)?
nodes.fail_action: Lagging buyer excluded so the seller still gets a bid or a generic unmatched.

nodes.question: Does the best bid minus margin still clear ($10 bid - $2 margin = $8 offer)?
nodes.fail_action: Stay on 'Yes'; the 'yes but sold non-exclusively' fallback can sell at a loss.

nodes.question: Did the vendor accept the $8 offer and the buyer return success on the post (30 s)?
nodes.pass_next: Post PII, bill the buyer, enforce a 15% refund cap over 30 days
nodes.fail_action: No PII is posted; read Show Lead Log bottom-up for 'price is missing' errors.

diagrams.title: The Call Network Flywheel
diagrams.subtitle: Buyer coverage attracts publishers; owned tracking holds the margin
diagrams.caption: Start as an affiliate sending calls into networks, load-balance across several, then go direct to buyers, because a network-to-direct jump is worth 100 to 300 points.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Network margins of 35-100% on average and 100-400% observed are Ringba masterclass figures; 8-12 applications for 4-6 acceptances is Ryan Moran's estimate. Team size is not quoted by practitioners.
diagrams.note: Sources: Ringba (20s5iGyl_MY, RhODbxB4ylU, AMwEMCOuhA0, Jvd7AeYwbns), ExclusiveLiveCall (Cu3vdN7Cn84), Ryan Moran (NC4s18S7p00).

center.role: Call broker owning tracking and routing
center.focus: Lock payout bumps in writing and never bluff a takeaway

spokes.kpi: 8-12 applications for 4-6 acceptances; a guaranteed concurrency figure
10 to 20-plus buyers per market; a $10 network call becomes $30-$80 direct
Separate sub IDs, conservative caps, paid on time after call review
Duplicate calls routed to different networks get paid twice for one caller

diagrams.title: Why Routing Method Sets the Payout
diagrams.subtitle: Divergent buyer payouts versus zip-level precision routing
diagrams.caption: Whoever owns the call tracking and routing layer owns the margin: divergent buyers rule out simultaneous dial, and zip-level routing lifted mortgage calls from $10 to up to $250.
diagrams.assumptions_note: The $10, $22 and $6 payouts are Adam of Ringba's example of buyers that should never share a simultaneous dial. The $10 to $250 lift is one Ringba mortgage client routing high home-value California zips. Duplicates run 5% to 25% of call flow and about 35% of people live outside their area code.
diagrams.note: Sources: Ringba / Adam (ojcbZuG798w), Ringba / Jordan Soto (yFkULiyenzk, 0eCCbtHmCJE).

buckets.label: Low-paying buyer in a split
buckets.notes: Route by priority and weight, not simultaneous dial.

buckets.label: Mid-paying buyer in a split
buckets.notes: East Coast and West Coast buyers need geo-accurate routing, not area code.

buckets.label: Top-paying buyer in a split
buckets.notes: Cap new buyers at $2,000 for the first 2 weeks until they pay.

buckets.label: Zip-level premium mortgage call
buckets.notes: Premium zips sold to smarter buyers; the rest dumped on networks.

diagrams.title: Deposit, Track, Reconcile, Then Scale
diagrams.subtitle: A four-step operating sequence for protecting the spread
diagrams.caption: The payout rate alone never proves a deal is profitable; rejected calls, duplicates, callback fraud, telecom costs and buyer credit risk all eat into the spread.
diagrams.assumptions_note: Week labels group practitioner gates into an operating order; practitioners did not prescribe a four-week schedule. Thresholds are attributed claims from John Ventura, ceohec, Ringba, TrackDrive, ExclusiveLiveCall and Marketcall.
diagrams.note: Sources: ceohec (SkS03nygdoY), Ringba (JxU9bgFTUUs), John Ventura (x3UYaJjRdx0, KeC4mKXnzs4), Marketcall (Dq9KUpYUWsE), TrackDrive (y8V08rKKNWY, yYZ5s6jFzQs), ExclusiveLiveCall (b7P50zcQzTs).

weeks.title: Collect deposits and sign the paper
weeks.deliverable: $500 to $1,000 minimum buyer deposit up front; QA addendum with a 50% penalty per CPA for callback fraud; signed affiliate one-pager.
weeks.gate: Always get payments up front before routing a call (ceohec).

weeks.title: Run tracked calls into a paid test
weeks.deliverable: Call tracker on every campaign; sell buyers a $2-5k test that reads out within 24-48 hours.
weeks.gate: No campaign runs without a call tracker (Marketcall).

weeks.title: Reconcile and dispute with specifics
weeks.deliverable: Pay publishers only on qualified calls; open disputes with dated specifics such as 'between the third and the seventh'.
weeks.gate: When 15 of 100 calls are disputed, find out why; a buyer failing to close is not an invalid call.

weeks.title: Scale only past the billable bar
weeks.deliverable: Billable rate at or above 50%, positive post-reconciliation margin, and clean QA.
weeks.gate: Add affiliates gradually and never 10 at once (John Ventura).
